title: Modal route lookup is disabled by default
evidence: Source: Flutter installs the modal route scope around route content (routes.dart:1188) and ModalRoute.of finds it (:1315). Incular RouteOutlet::new sets modal_route_scopes to false (route_outlet.rs:465); content_widget installs ModalRoute only when set_modal_route_scopes(true) was called (:980-986). No frame scenario: the frame harness cannot drive a RouteOutlet.
impact: Route content that calls ModalRoute::of under a default RouteOutlet sees no route until the application opts in.
cause: Modal route scope installation is an opt-in outlet policy rather than an always-present route scope.
fix_direction: Make the default outlet install the modal route scope, or document the opt-in as the supported contract with a construction-time default that matches Flutter's lookup expectations.
limitations: Source only; the opt-in may be intentional for outlets that host no ModalRoute consumers.

title: Imperative stack removal and predicate operations are missing
evidence: Source: Flutter NavigatorState exposes pushAndRemoveUntil (navigator.dart:5247), popUntil (:5635), removeRoute (:5677) and removeRouteBelow (:5702). Incular Navigator exposes push (navigator.rs:421), maybe_pop and pop (:770, :818), and replace (:826); set_pages (:661) reconciles a whole page list. No predicate-based or identity-based removal method exists (rg for remove_route, pop_until and push_and_remove_until found none).
impact: Applications cannot remove a specific route under the top route or pop to a named route, for example when replacing a login flow with a new root route.
cause: Incular models stack changes as whole-list reconciliation plus top-only operations rather than Flutter's imperative route-predicate methods.
fix_direction: Add route-identity and predicate removal operations with explicit guard, lifecycle and observer semantics matching Flutter's order.
limitations: Code reading only; set_pages can express some of these outcomes but was not compared as an equivalent.

title: PageRouteBuilder does not create Flutter's default route animations
scenario: navigation__navigator__fade_pop_timeline (push timing: navigation__navigator__fade_push_timeline, matches within a 1.3 ms harness residual)
evidence: Source as before. Scenario: fade_pop_timeline with Flutter reverseTransitionDuration 300 ms keeps the popped route present at 400 ms; Incular removes it at the pop, so probe.top.present diverges from frame 25. Forward fade timing matches within the harness residual.
impact: Code driven by the route's primary or secondary animation (including hero flights on default page transitions) has no default timeline to observe.
cause: Incular's transition is an optional paint composition, while Flutter's route always owns its transition controllers.
fix_direction: Keep primary and secondary route animation controllers with Flutter's default and reverse durations even when the transition paints no motion.
limitations: Code reading only. A frame twin needs a Navigator-hosting harness (see the findings md harness requests).

title: Overlay entries lack per-entry removal and rebuild lifecycle
evidence: Source: Flutter OverlayEntry.remove and markNeedsBuild (overlay.dart:225, :247) and OverlayState insert-relative and rearrange (:718, :789). Incular Overlay::insert appends (presentation.rs:666), remove_top and dismiss_top act only on the top entry (:675, :680), and OverlayEntry has no removal handle or rebuild method (:569).
impact: An application cannot update or remove one persistent overlay entry while keeping the others, or ask one entry to rebuild after its builder state changes.
cause: Incular's Overlay is a stack value, not a retained entry lifecycle with stable entry identity.
fix_direction: Give entries stable identity and per-entry remove, rebuild and ordering operations.
limitations: Code reading only; OverlayPortal covers the widget-level show and hide path separately.

title: Hero flights do not run on normal route pops
evidence: Source and existing test as before. Scenario: Flutter keeps the destination route through its reverse flight (probe hero_to present at 400 ms); Incular removes it at the pop. Hero flight geometry is not compared: Flutter flight copies the probed child, so probe rects report destination geometry (harness request).
impact: Shared-tag heroes disappear with the popped route instead of flying back to their origin during ordinary back navigation.
cause: A popped route is discarded at commit rather than kept mounted through its reverse transition.
fix_direction: Keep the popped route mounted through its reverse transition and let the hero controller observe the reverse animation before disposal.
limitations: Source and existing test; no frame twin because the frame harness cannot drive a Navigator. Pop flights through a user gesture are not in scope.

title: Router back dispatch cannot transfer priority to nested Routers
evidence: Source: Flutter's Router creates child dispatchers and supports takePriority, deferTo and forget (router.dart:1021-1084, :1125-1149). Incular's RouterConfig::with_back_button_dispatcher accepts only the app-shell RootBackButtonDispatcher (router.rs:866); that type holds a newest-first callback list (:635-685) and shares it through dispatcher() (:740-746), with no child creation or priority transfer. Separate navigation BackButtonDispatcher has create_child (back_dispatch.rs:413-420) and defer_to (:423-428), but the Router does not accept it.
impact: Nested Routers cannot hand back-button priority to a child Router through RouterConfig; the child-priority mechanism exists only on a dispatcher type the Router cannot use.
cause: App-shell Router back dispatch and navigation pop-scope dispatch use separate dispatcher types.
fix_direction: Add child dispatchers with explicit priority transfer and parent fallback to the Router's dispatcher type, or accept the navigation dispatcher in RouterConfig.
limitations: Code reading only; no back-event scenario because the frame recorder has no back-button event input.

title: OverlayPortal popup pictures are culled by an ancestor clip
evidence: Pixel: overlay_portal_no_clip matches at 1x; with the only scene change being a ClipRect around the 80x80 anchor, the 40x40 orange popup at (110,110) appears in Flutter and is absent in Incular (6.25% of the 160x160 image). Frame: content_outside_anchor_clip matches geometry and tap, so the popup layout is correct and the loss is in paint. Source at HEAD: flatten_layer_contents culls a Picture outside the active clip (compositor.rs:1590) before paint lifts surface partitions (painting.rs:146-164). The pixel scene was not re-run at HEAD in this pass (orchestrator-owned Windows pixel harness); the mechanism was re-read at HEAD and the code is unchanged apart from exact_copy in the picture update path.
impact: An OverlayPortal popup disappears when it extends beyond an ancestor ClipRect, including clips that bound an anchor or viewport.
cause: Compositor flattening applies the ancestor clip to the popup's Picture descendants before the partition lift can detach them.
fix_direction: Preserve surface-partition descendants through ancestor-clip culling and apply clipping from the popup's own subtree after lifting.
limitations: Pixel evidence is at 1x only and predates HEAD; re-run overlay_portal_ancestor_clip in the pixel harness before closing.

title: RouteOutlet rejects routes that present overlay entries
evidence: Source: Flutter's OverlayRoute installs its overlay entries into the Overlay while the route is on the stack (routes.dart:55). Incular Route::overlay (presentation.rs:106) builds RoutePresentation::Overlay, and OutletPlacement::of classifies it as ExternalOverlay (route_outlet.rs:92-94). The test outlet_rejects_overlay_routes_explicitly asserts that RouteOutlet::present_frame returns an error for such a stack and leaves state unchanged.
impact: A Navigator stack containing an overlay route makes the outlet frame fail with a typed error instead of showing the route's entries. Applications must place overlay content outside the navigator.
cause: Overlay content is portal-managed by design, and the outlet does not host route-owned overlay entries; the rejection is intentional to avoid silent omission.
fix_direction: Host route-owned overlay entries through the outlet's overlay host, or state the supported alternative explicitly in the Route::overlay API documentation.
limitations: Flutter's OverlayRoute is a base class that apps rarely subclass directly; ModalRoute-style routes are covered separately. The rejection is documented and tested, so it may be an accepted design boundary.
verified_by: orchestrator package rerun (scenario-backed) or independent source verification (source-only); see VERIFICATION.md and verification-source-findings.md

title: OverlayPortal replaces the caller key on its anchor child
flutter_ref: widgets/overlay.dart:2023-2038 (widget.child passed through unchanged, only wrapped in Semantics)
evidence: With the anchor probe as the direct OverlayPortal child, Flutter records the anchor at frame 0 (rect 0,0 100x100 under the tight SizedBox) and Incular records no anchor probe in any frame. The cause is source-level: OverlayPortal wraps its child with with_key(OVERLAY_PORTAL_ANCHOR_KEY) in both the shown and hidden stacks (navigation_scopes.rs:190, :229), which replaces any key the child already has. With the probe wrapped inside an Align, the same scene matches (show_hide and content_outside_anchor_clip), so the divergence comes from the key override and not from the portal's geometry.
impact: A caller key on an OverlayPortal child is ignored, so changing that key does not recreate the child and external lookups by that key fail. Anchor state is still preserved because the internal key is constant.
cause: The portal uses the child's key slot for its own anchor identity instead of wrapping the child in an outer keyed element.
fix_direction: Wrap the anchor in an internal keyed element (or give the anchor an outer key) so the caller key survives, as Flutter does.
limitations: The harness probe is itself a key, so the scenario observes the override only through the probe; user-visible impact is limited to key-driven recreation or lookup. Confidence is medium because the impact is inferred from the source, not from a caller that depends on the key.
verified_by: orchestrator package rerun (scenario-backed) or independent source verification (source-only); see VERIFICATION.md and verification-source-findings.md

title: Covered route is hidden from the first frame of a fade push
flutter_ref: widgets/navigator.dart (the route below stays painted while the top route animates in)
evidence: Scenario: at the first frame after a 300 ms fade push, the below route probe is opacity 1.0 in Flutter and 0.0 in Incular, and stays 0.0 for the transition. Source: the occlusion loop treats a route as settled when route_animation() is None (presentation.rs:539-543 returns None for Fade), so a fading route occludes the route below at once; route_outlet.rs:894-907 comments that the route below shows while animating in. The zero-duration PopScope and observer scenarios show the same early hide under an opaque route, which is not visible there.
impact: Fade page transitions blank the page underneath for the whole fade instead of revealing it.
cause: Fade transitions have no RouteAnimation, so the outlet treats them as completed when deciding occlusion.
fix_direction: Treat a fading route as not settled while its opacity controller runs (check the controller status, not only the RouteAnimation variant).
limitations: Flutter secondary-animation reading is unresolved: the probe reads 1.0 where the transitionsBuilder should lower the below route toward 0.5, so the exact below-route opacity target is unverified; the occlusion timing divergence stands on its own.
verified_by: orchestrator package rerun (scenario-backed) or independent source verification (source-only); see VERIFICATION.md and verification-source-findings.md

title: Navigator has no TransitionDelegate for declarative page changes
evidence: Flutter lets declarative (pages-based) navigation decide per route whether page additions and removals animate (markForPush/markForAdd/markForPop/markForComplete/markForRemove). Incular exposes no such hook.
impact: Apps cannot control which declarative page-list changes animate, for example to add pages without a push animation or remove them without a pop transition.
fix_direction: Add a transition-delegate hook to page-based navigation with Flutter's default decisions.
limitations: Source only; Incular's default animation decisions for page-list diffs were not compared.
